agent.name: Emerging Technology Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Context-sensitive adoption posture, evidence thresholds and reversibility

analytical_question: Within a six-week evidence-gathering horizon, should a hypothetical U.S. online homeware retailer with two marketing staff and an owner approver use text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the reference architecture, for internal advertising concepts and mood boards? The decision concerns a reversible internal evaluation, not final product photography, public advertising, or company approval.
general_et_finding: Historical observation: Stable Diffusion was publicly released in August 2022. Supplied surveys show use of broad AI among U.S. businesses and creative generative AI among surveyed international creators, but neither measures repeated text-to-image mood-board use among comparable small U.S. homeware retailers. The target workflow's diffusion stage remains unclassified. Rogers supplies a framework for assessing relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability, not a current adoption rate. Historical availability does not verify a presently selected model's architecture, capabilities, license or input-use terms. These findings remain unchanged by organizational adoption posture.
application_finding: Plausible inference: generating disposable internal visual directions could support exploration before a photo shoot, and existing image-editing and catalogue-comparison skills may help staff assess outputs. Relative advantage remains unmeasured. Evaluation must include briefing, prompting, selection, correction, catalogue fidelity checks, owner review and accepted boards, rather than generation speed alone. The comparator is the existing catalogue-reference, manual-board and freelance-designer process; existing licensed design tools are another option if their relevant conditions are established. Product appearance errors, unsupported brand references and review burden could eliminate any benefit. Final photography and copy require separate authorship and checking.
organization_specific_finding: Case assumptions establish two marketing staff, an owner who approves concepts, no internal ML capability or training compute, and an aggressive preference for reversible internal learning. Evaluating an already trained model avoids a training requirement, but vendor suitability and permissions remain unresolved. Discardable internal concepts and no automatic publication make bounded exposure plausible; limited staff capacity makes evaluation hours a material opportunity cost. The aggressive posture supports gathering matched-peer evidence alongside proposal preparation without requiring peer success before trial authorization. It does not authorize tool use, uploads or publication.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No local or tightly matched evidence establishes repeatable net value after prompting, correction, review and accepted output.
Broad AI and creator surveys have unmatched populations and measures; their rates cannot classify the target workflow's diffusion stage.
Vendor, version, architecture, price, license, input rights, retention and output-use conditions remain unresolved. Unknown permission is not a discovered prohibition.
Manual boards and freelance design may already deliver sufficient variety and fidelity with less staff burden.
Discardability limits exposure only while concepts remain internal and controlled; accidental publication or misleading product depictions would increase consequences.
The proposed staff-hour cap and comparison design are management proposals, not measured benefits, approved resources or completed tests.
The contrast assessments below are reasoning checks within this response, not independent blind runs or observed organizational outcomes.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the distinction between historical availability, broad uptake and unclassified workflow-specific diffusion, conditional on the supplied cards. Moderate confidence that a reversible comparative trial is a reasonable proposal given the hypothetical case constraints. Low confidence in realized time savings, cost savings, output fidelity or sustained usability because none has been measured locally. Current vendor permissions and model suitability are unresolved. Schema compliance and contrast reasoning do not establish real-world effectiveness.
value_opportunity_implication: The opportunity is useful visual exploration before commissioning photography. Compare matched briefs against the existing manual/designer workflow, recording total staff time through owner acceptance, designer review effort, direct tool costs, accepted distinct visual directions and product-fidelity defects. Record rejected outputs and abandoned briefs so selection does not hide effort. No saving or revenue effect can presently be claimed. If quality is comparable but total effort rises without a documented improvement in useful exploration, the existing process remains preferable.
risk_governance_implication: Before any execution, establish owner authorization, a suitable vendor and version, applicable account and output-use rights, and permission for every proposed input. Review retention and training-use conditions before uploads; use only approved, non-sensitive, rights-cleared material. Keep concepts internal and visibly identified as exploratory, retain provenance and review records, and check catalogue fidelity and unsupported brand references. Trial authorization must exclude automatic publication and final advertising approval. Stop execution on an input-rights concern, unexpected disclosure, uncontrolled distribution or exhaustion of the effort cap. These are proposed boundaries, not legal clearance or a certification of controls.
recommendation_management_implication: BOUNDED_EXPERIMENT. This means prepare and seek authorization for a trial; no trial is approved or started. It yields more justified learning than MONITOR because a low-consequence manual comparison is plausible. ADOPT_IMPLEMENT lacks demonstrated local value and cleared permissions. PROOF_OF_CONCEPT is not the leading choice because workflow value, rather than an identified technical feasibility barrier, is the primary uncertainty. A: NOW, without model execution or uploads, document the existing process and baseline, prepare matched briefs and a written comparison proposal, investigate current vendor conditions, and seek comparable-peer evidence. These preparation activities require neither completed peer proof nor trial approval. B: PERMISSION, before execution, requires owner approval of scope and resources, verified vendor/input-use conditions, internal-only handling and review boundaries. Propose at most three paired briefs and 12 total incremental staff-hours, including prompting, selection, editing, review and recording, plus an explicitly approved direct-spend limit. Compare with the existing manual/designer process using total time to accepted board, accepted useful directions, fidelity defects, rework, reviewer effort and actual cost. Acceptability criteria must be agreed before execution and must preserve required fidelity; stop for permission concerns, uncontrolled exposure, the hour cap, or repeated fidelity failures that cannot be corrected within it. If these conditions cannot be met, remain at proposal only. C: LATER, wider adoption requires repeatable acceptable results across the paired briefs, evidence that any advantage survives all review and correction costs, continuing rights and resource suitability, and a separate owner decision. Conservative posture-only contrast: retain the same no-tool preparation step, but require credible, workflow-matched peer evidence of repeated use and documented review burden before authorizing an actual local trial; a peer account may inform the threshold but cannot supply a market denominator. High-consequence application contrast: if outputs instead become unreviewed public product advertising, recommend REJECT_FOR_NOW for that configuration because misleading product appearance and uncontrolled publication conflict with the required boundaries. A redesigned workflow with verified product accuracy and separate approval is a separate decision. The strongest upward reversal condition is repeatable owner-accepted boards meeting predefined fidelity requirements with a documented net advantage over the manual comparator and cleared permissions; an inability to establish those permissions blocks execution.
change_monitoring_triggers: During the six-week horizon and before any execution decision, verify the selected vendor, version, relevant architecture, current terms, input rights, data handling and direct-spend limit. Unresolved conditions keep the work at proposal only.

Before trial authorization, confirm that the proposed paired briefs, fidelity criteria, manual comparator, review responsibilities and 12 incremental staff-hour cap are feasible with two marketing staff.

If an authorized trial occurs within the horizon, review time, accepted directions, rework and fidelity after each paired brief. Stop at the cap or immediately upon a permission or distribution failure.

By the end of week six, present the baseline, permission status, any authorized comparative results and remaining uncertainty for a separate continuation decision. The horizon creates no deployment deadline.

During proposal preparation and at the six-week review, seek evidence from small U.S. online homeware retailers of repeated internal concept-board use during the preceding three months. Record population, workflow, review burden and denominator where available; absent a matched denominator and timeline, retain the unclassified diffusion-stage judgment.

Reassess immediately if scope changes from internal exploration to public advertising, sensitive inputs, automatic publication or materially greater financial exposure; internal-trial findings do not authorize the changed use.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Before execution, identify the proposed vendor/model/version and verify current account, input-use, retention and output-use conditions; these determine whether the proposed trial can be authorized.
Obtain owner approval for scope, incremental staff hours, direct spending and review boundaries. These are execution gates, not prerequisites for drafting the proposal.
Establish the existing process's total effort and accepted-output criteria, including freelance-designer involvement, to make comparative results decision-relevant.
Clarify which catalogue images and brand materials may be used and what product-fidelity defects make a concept unacceptable.
Abstain from assigning a precise market diffusion stage, certifying product accuracy, granting legal clearance or recommending wider implementation on the supplied evidence.
Hand off ownership, staffing allocation, workflow integration, training and scaling design to the Organizational Adoption Agent if management elects to develop the proposal further.
